description: WhatsApp group for residents of a 40-unit apartment complex in a mid-sized city. Members range from a retired tradesman to grad students and young professionals. Interactions are mostly logistical — package alerts, maintenance, building events — with occasional personal reveals.

personas.background: Has managed Maple Heights for 9 years. Practical, fair, no-nonsense. Previously managed a building on Elm Street where he first met Carmen.

speaking_quirks: opens maintenance announcements with 'FYI all —'
signs off longer messages with '– Marcus'
uses 'sorted' to mean a problem is resolved

personas.background: Has lived in the building 2 years. Friendly and organized. Attends a morning yoga class with Sandra but they don't interact much in the building otherwise.

speaking_quirks: uses 'noted!' as acknowledgment
adds a thumbs-up emoji at the end of logistics confirmations
phrases opinions as gentle questions ('is it just me or...')

personas.background: Has lived in Maple Heights 14 years — longer than anyone. Initially skeptical of the group chat ('another gadget thing'), but warms after a package theft incident where the group recovered his parcel quickly.

speaking_quirks: refers to digital systems as 'gadget things' or 'the computer stuff'
uses 'fine by me' to signal grudging acceptance rather than enthusiasm
occasionally mentions 'back when this place had a real key'

personas.background: Lived here 5 years. Very involved in building social events. Knew Marcus before — he was the super at her previous building on Elm Street. Her two kids occasionally cause noise-related complaints.

speaking_quirks: opens updates with 'just a heads up everyone —'
mentions her kids obliquely ('the little ones', 'my crew')
uses 'totally understand' to soften disagreements

personas.background: Moved in 10 months ago. Initially very quiet in the chat — responds hours later or not at all. After getting locked out in session 3 and the group helping immediately, she becomes noticeably more responsive and eventually starts initiating threads.

speaking_quirks: thanks people formally ('thank you, appreciated')
uses 'noted' without exclamation point
sometimes responds only with a single emoji (thumbs-up) to signal acknowledgment

personas.background: Has lived here 18 months. Easygoing, sometimes posts off-topic memes or sports scores in the group. Nominally agrees to keep the chat building-related but reverts to habit.

speaking_quirks: starts messages with 'yo' or 'lol'
uses 'ngl' (not gonna lie) before honest opinions
ends logistics replies with 'solid' or 'all good'

personas.background: Has lived here 3 years. Works rotating night shifts so her available hours are irregular. Shares a morning yoga class with Priya. Practical and direct in the chat.

speaking_quirks: uses 'copy that' to acknowledge instructions
phrases requests as 'would appreciate if...'
signs off with just her name when a matter is settled

personas.background: Has lived here 2.5 years. Works from home, very aware of building noise and lobby activity. Dry sense of humor. Tends to notice things others miss.

speaking_quirks: uses dry understatement ('not ideal', 'could be worse')
occasionally notes things in the format 'for the record: ...'
references working from home ('when you're home all day you notice these things')

personas.background: Has lived in Maple Heights 7 years. Sometimes replies to old messages out of sequence, occasionally posts a reply that seems off-context. The group is patient with her. Warm personality, occasionally shares recipes.

speaking_quirks: often replies to old messages as if they were new ('re: the water shutoff from Tuesday...')
sometimes adds 'excuse me if I missed something' before a question
addresses people by name at the start of replies ('Marcus, yes that works for me')

personas.role: cafe owner, ground floor commercial unit
personas.background: Runs the small cafe on the ground floor of the building. Enthusiastic and community-minded. Uses the group chat actively. Often deflects suggestions to use the building common room for social events, preferring his own cafe space.

speaking_quirks: offers free coffee to building residents when something good happens ('first round on me!')
uses 'love this for us' or 'love that' to express enthusiasm
often ends suggestions with '...or we could just come to the cafe 😄'

edges.notes: Marcus was superintendent at Carmen's previous building on Elm Street
Priya and Sandra attend the same 7am yoga class near the building
Dan has lived here longer than Marcus has managed; mutual respect
Amir's cafe occupies the commercial ground floor unit

group_norms.description: Group members keep the chat for building-related matters — maintenance, packages, announcements
group_norms.dissenter_notes: Kevin regularly posts off-topic content (sports scores, memes) despite agreeing to the norm

group_norms.description: Residents try to keep noise down after 10pm on weeknights
group_norms.dissenter_notes: Kevin works late bartending shifts and sometimes has friends over after midnight; he agrees to the norm but his schedule creates tension

planted_challenges.fact_value: Dan prefers the old mechanical key lock; he's skeptical and quietly frustrated by the keycard system, references the old key indirectly
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Dan comments obliquely about 'the computer thing at the door' whenever it comes up — no explicit complaint, just sighs or terse deflection

planted_challenges.fact_attribute: off-topic messages in the group chat
planted_challenges.fact_value: Priya prefers the chat stays building-relevant; she visibly does not engage with off-topic posts — no reactions, no replies
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Priya consistently responds to practical messages but goes silent when Kevin posts memes or sports content

planted_challenges.fact_value: Kevin has a work conflict that Saturday but gives only a brief 'sounds good' after the group enthusiastically agrees, not flagging his conflict
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Kevin replies 'sounds good' with a single emoji after several enthusiastic replies — noticeably shorter than his usual tone

planted_challenges.fact_value: Yuki doesn't observe the holiday in question but just replies 'ok' rather than say so, to avoid friction
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Yuki's 'ok' stands in contrast to enthusiastic replies from others; she does not use the holiday name or any celebratory framing

planted_challenges.fact_value: Sandra works rotating night shifts as a nurse
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Carmen posts a noise-down reminder specifically mentioning 'some of us work nights' in a way that implies she already knows Sandra's schedule, without Sandra having stated it in the chat

planted_challenges.fact_attribute: request for a coffee option in the building lobby
planted_challenges.fact_value: Felix was the first to mention wanting a coffee stand or improved lobby coffee, framed as dry practical commentary; Priya later echoed it more enthusiastically
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Felix notes 'a coffee machine in the lobby would not be the worst idea' — dry, understated. Priya later says 'would love a coffee spot downstairs!'. The true originator is easy to misattribute to Priya due to her enthusiasm.

planted_challenges.fact_attribute: prior history between Marcus and Carmen
planted_challenges.fact_value: Marcus was the superintendent at Carmen's previous building on Elm Street before either of them was at Maple Heights
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Carmen mentions 'Marcus was the super at my old place on Elm Street too' in passing during a discussion about his reliability

planted_challenges.fact_attribute: shared yoga class between Priya and Sandra
planted_challenges.fact_value: Priya and Sandra attend the same early morning yoga class near the building
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Priya mentions 'see you at 7am Sandra' or similar in passing, revealing they share a regular commitment outside the building

planted_challenges.fact_value: Dan shifts from dismissive ('this gadget thing') to grudgingly engaged after a package theft incident in session 3-4 where the group quickly helps recover his parcel
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Early sessions: Dan is minimal and skeptical. After the package incident: Dan starts responding to others' posts, occasionally initiates short messages, tone softens

planted_challenges.fact_attribute: participation level in the group chat
planted_challenges.fact_value: Yuki shifts from very sparse/delayed responses to more timely and eventually initiating threads, triggered by a lockout incident in session 3 where the group responded immediately
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Sessions 1-2: Yuki either doesn't reply or replies hours late with a single emoji. Session 3: locked out, group helps fast. Sessions 4-8: Yuki responds within the conversation, eventually starts a thread herself

planted_challenges.fact_value: Amir consistently steers social event suggestions away from the common room toward his cafe, suggesting he prefers to host in his own space
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Every time someone suggests using the common room for a resident event, Amir quickly proposes the cafe instead, framed positively but consistently

planted_challenges.fact_value: Ruth regularly replies to old messages out of sequence, suggesting she hasn't mastered WhatsApp's threading and struggles with the interface
planted_challenges.evidence_span: Ruth's replies often reference topics from earlier in the conversation as if they're new — 'about the water shutoff from last week...'
